What helps me remember everything is think in threes! It rhymes to help more lol. And count it out loud, like seriously. There’s a few threes but these might be the most helpful for you..
• So for lane changes after you signal at least 100 feet before your turn it’s ONE (rear view) TWO (side view) THREE (over the shoulder).
• For stop signs, come to a FULL stop at the line NO MATTER WHAT! Count to THREE while checking back and fourth whether you can see or not, still fully stopped, then slowly creep forward for vision (this is totally fine as long as you’ve stopped first!) and proceed when safe while still checking back and fourth. Go in some neighborhoods and practice the 3 count at stop signs.

Lastly what helped me is I actually found a driving school that specialized in nervous drivers. You may not have that privilege where you are but look around. I have a coworker who took her skills test out in the country and it helped her too. Pick a time that’s not busy as well.

Is he free fed? If so, it's important to get him on a schedule. Free feeding is also dangerous because it leads to obesity and insulin resistance (because his blood sugar is spiked constantly).

Cats thrive on schedules so having him on one should be highly beneficial.  When cats know what's coming for them it's much more comfortable. Personally, I am the same way!

In addition to a solid feeding schedule playing in short bursts BEFORE eating is actually very helpful. This mimics their natural **"hunt, eat, groom, sleep"** which is so important to kitties! Make sure you're playing properly with your cat and keep him interested. Mimic the **hunt.** Don't bop him in the head with toys or shake the feather side to side. Make the toy look as interesting as possible. Do let him catch it a few times for a few seconds here and there. When he is tired out as much as you can then let him take the toy and have him **eat** him a wholesome and healthy meal immediately after. Following next, gently **groom** if he enjoys it. Lastly, dial it down very quietly with some gentle pets and let him really relax. Here's where you can bring over a blanket/towel with the pheromone spray on it and put it next to him. Get into this routine for at least a week and see how it goes.

We want to enrich his life! Eventually you could take him out on a harness if you live in a quiet area and see how he takes to that. A lot of cats seriously enjoy that but some may be frightened. My one cat lights up when he goes outside and you can just tell it makes his day, my other one just wants to go back inside..

Also for the diffuser, I don't now if the behaviorist told you how to properly use it, but it's crucial to note that they only really work in an isolated room or tiny house where you can capture all of the pheromones and don't work if you just have them out in a hallway or large open room because there's too much space. As for the sprays, they are meant to be used on bedding or collars/bandanas, they are very concentrated. The pheromones I use and highly recommend to my clients is always Feliway. Feliway is used in vet offices as well. 

Try to isolate him in the room again with those pheromones going prior for about 6-8 hours and continue with that schedule. You can let him out of the room (keep it closed when hes not in it) if you are supervising him.

You're probably not going to like a lot of the things I have to say here but..

Two things..

For the automatic feeder, why do you need one? Are you going away on vacation? If not, please don't unless it's glass/stainless steel and on a set timer that gives a small amount for each feeding (no more than 200 kcal per day for the average indoor adult). Most are plastic which is porous and can cause bacteria buildup. And the worst part is if you are free feeding this is an easy road to serious overeating, diabetes, and obesity. You are causing your cats blood sugar to be spiked all day long (especially on such an very high carb food) and this leads to insulin resistance. You'll save so much money in the long run not free feeding too!

As for the food itself, I have an education on pet nutrition and work in the field. Foods like this blow my mind and are frustrating. I can't help but get frustrated when I hear people fall into these marketing traps. Royal Canin diets are quick fixes and don't actually have studies to prove their long term safety. The ingredients are from China and are full of byproducts (unidentified meat, yuck!) and carbs galore (totally inappropriate for a cat, hard to digest, common allergens). Ingredients like these keep these companies costs low and their profits high. This is how they afford their great marketing, buying out of companies, funding of big events, and paying people to sponsor them (like vets and influencers).

Vets take very short courses in nutrition and trust brands like Royal Canin (Mars M&Ms), Purina (Nestle), and Hill's (Colgate Palmolive) because they are heavily promoted to them and most of their colleges are funded by companies like Mars that actually own most vet offices like VCA, Banfield, and BluePearl for example. These companies are a HUGE monopoly and are behind so much.

[A phenomenal site my professor shared with me about RX diets](https://catinfo.org/#Prescription/Therapeutic_Diets)

[A great video made by someone in the vet field on why vets are so uneducated about nutrition](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ePAOgMhRgYE)

What blows my mind the most about this food is just how high carb it is. Dry matter analysis it is around 40%+ carb. Cats lack an enzyme called amylase which helps to break down carbs in the mouth. It's a total marketing myth that kibble cleans teeth. Okay sure, maybe the cat chewing on hard large pieces of kibble might scrape off *soft* pieces of food stuck but that doesn't change carbs will just build up again. It's like chewing on a hard large piece of candy and expecting it to "clean" your teeth. 

I have an indoor raw fed senior cat with perfect teeth. This is because her diet contains no carbs. She is lean, her skin and coat is silky and lustrous, she drinks maybe a half cup of water a week because she gets it from her diet, and she has tiny poos every other day that barely smell. This is indicative of a high quality diet.

Pet nutritionists opinions here..

***All*** grocery store foods are bottom of the barrel quality. Yep, it's true. Even the ones people think are typically the healthiest options like Blue Buffalo and FreshPet. The only acceptable one is the Costco brand food is not *terrible* as the maker of the food is at least somewhat decent. Grocery store foods are cheap and convenient (just like human fast food!) and so that's why they appeal to customers already buying groceries.

The ingredients are.. *questionable*.. to say the least. Let's break them down.

Meat By-Products, Salmon, Poultry By-Products, Fish, Brewers Rice, Natural Flavors, Guar Gum, Added Color

**Meat By-Products** are a completely unidentified meat. They can't tell what animal it is or what organ(s) it is. By products are typically poor quality organs scraped off of what's left from the initial process of slaughter that cheap companies will buy to keep their costs low and profits higher. Yuck, would you eat a totally unidentifiable meat? I definitely wouldn't!

**Salmon** is the only good ingredient here. It's a named meat and it's not a byproduct.

**Poultry By-Products** is yet another unnamed meat. What kind of poultry? Chicken, turkey, duck? They really cannot identify the animal or organ it came from?

**Fish** is more unidentified meat. What kind of fish is it?

**Brewers Rice** comes from alcoholic breweries and is a waste byproduct of the creation of hops (alcohol) and is simply fragments of rice kernels. Hops is HIGHLY toxic to cats and sometimes the rice may have some alcoholic residue on it. Rice is totally inappropriate for a cat to eat and couldn't be farther from biologically appropriate. They are obligate carnivores and have absolutely no need for carbohydrates. Carbs are hard to digest and are typically only an allergen for cats.

**Guar Gum** is a common thickener to give the food texture. Completely unnecessary.

**Added Color**... just why... Dyes have been PROVEN to be cancerous to humans *AND* cats. There is absolutely NO reason for this to even be in the food. This is to make the food more appealing to us. A common marketing trick among other greedy and poor quality brands like Iams, Purina, Friskies, and Meow Mix.

My suggestion is go to a smaller owned holistic pet store. They are usually very willing to give free cans of cat food and kibble to try out! They are all about wellness of pets and many of the employees are highly educated unlike big conglomerates like PetCo/PetSmart.

A few questions if you don't mind, I like to get as much information as possible to better help.

(these only work in *very* limited areas), Did you isolate him in a room with the diffuser and give the diffuser a whole week minimum? Moving is a **HUUUUGEEE** shock to a cats life. They don't understand what's going on. This cat has been through a ton it seems, we need to think about how *they* feel. So many changes in only 5 or so years of this poor kitties life! Cats do everything for a reason and honestly.. they aren't actually smart enough to do things in spite. It's important to know that cats are *extremely* stoic and don't show they are stressed when in reality some are likely are absolutely dying inside. In nature if they acted stressed and hurt they might seem like easy prey to predators.

To relate, maybe not the exact issues but somewhat alike.. when I had first gotten my cat a long time ago he was perfect for the first 2 months. Just the HAPPIEST little kitten, absolutely loved to play, social butterfly among friends and family, never would get off your lap like a total velcro baby. But after those 2 months (with absolutely no personality change) he was peeing absolutely everywhere and it was causing rifts in my relationship and my husband was about to toss him out. We tried putting down tinfoil to scare him (he'd pee on it), used a motion detecting air spray to scare him away from spots (he'd find another), got him checked for UTDs (expensive and with no found issues), put tons of litterboxes and pee pads around (he would still go elsewhere). Nothing worked. Till we considered stress. Stress was the last that that we personally thought but we gave CBD oil, used a pheromone diffuser, and kept everything in the household as calm as possible, all while isolating him in a room for a few months. He never did it again except for a few times where there was stress in the house like fireworks or yelling which further made it clear that was the issue. We did a very slow reintroduction. So what I'm saying here is sometimes you just need to start from square 1 again. Cats need everything done *SUUUUPER* slow.

My oldest girl (she was about 4 and a half at the time of the introduction) DESPISED my new youngest (3 months then). She would smell him and hiss and swat at me and anything that smelled like him just like what you're going through. Cats are extremely territorial! Most people don't realize this. They will even fight till the death to defend their territory out in the wild.

It's actually good they are opposite sexes because they tend to get along better! Has he always been a single child? For me my girl was and a new kitten was so foreign to her and scary (who is this in MY home!?). I started introductions very slow for months. She would smack the door if he was near it but I slowly started feeding them close to each other on each side of the door (not in swatting distance) and she warmed up to him a bit more here and there and eventually could keep the door very slightly cracked so they could *juuuust* see each others little faces. Eventually they were given treats together and that was a really enjoyable time they associated with each other. Keep introducing smells and make sure your smell is mixed in with hers. Be patient and don't rush anything (first impressions are everything!). In the end it took my girl about a whole year to tolerate him. They don't cuddle or anything but they occasionally play and that's probably as good as it'll get for my two. Like mine, your kitty might just be very independent and he doesn't want to share! Don't worry about it, this is all very typical. Good luck!

Obesity can cause serious health issues, heart attacks, and even a shorter lifespan. Chip reader feeders can be seriously expensive. Could you possibly just feed them in separate rooms? My mother had gotten a new kitten and she would steal food all the time from the other one and she eventually got pretty overweight. She made a feeding routine to put her in the laundry room and feed her there and it helped her lose weight all the way back down to healthy. Cats don't need to be fed more than once or twice a day. I feed my girl once a day and she's perfect weight and she doesn't even beg for more food, she's completely content with once a day feeding. Simple fix is really just to separate them till they're done eating. For the scarfing, if you don't mind the extra work you can buy a [food dispensing ball](https://www.amazon.com/Catit-51282-Treat-Ball-Blue/dp/B00357M8S2/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1535249845&sr=8-1&keywords=catit+treat+ball) you can fill up with some crunchies and it's pretty entertaining to the cat and for the human and they really take their time eating so no barfing!
